title: Meta Just Released a Free AI Agent That Runs on One GPU
description:
Meta just open-sourced its 30B agent model — free, Apache 2.0, and it runs on ONE GPU. We break down the benchmark table, the politics behind the release, and the one table where Qwen still wins.

We covered the rogue-agent breach that slipped through OpenAI's systems in the video below — the same week this model dropped. Watch them together.

Meta released Muse Glimmer on August 10, 2026, three days after its flagship Muse Spark went on API-only lockdown. It is a 30B vision-language agent — the open-weights distilled version of Spark — distributed under Apache 2.0 with the full instruction-tuned weights on Hugging Face.

The part that changes the economics: priced at roughly $0.10 per million tokens on Meta's own API, and fully runnable at home. The 55GB full-precision model needs a hefty card, but the 24GB quantized version runs on a single consumer GPU at 233 tokens/second. Not demo speed — that's faster than most of us generate.

Where it lands on the leaderboard: 75.5 on MCP Atlas (vs Gemma 54 and Qwen 62), 74.6 DeepSearch QA, 51.2 SWE-Bench Pro, and 94.7 on AIME. But the honest catch — Qwen's 3.6 still wins GDPVal, OSWorld, and SWE-Bench Verified. This is a genuinely competitive field now, and the gap is close.

Timeline: full model this week on Hugging Face, the Spark 1.2 update before the end of the year.
